class.name: GLTFItem
class.brief_description: Base class for all glTF item classes.
class.description: GLTFItem is a minimal base class, common to all classes that represent the data of glTF items found in glTF files. This includes nodes, meshes, materials, textures, and animations. GLTFItem classes can be serialized to a [Dictionary] using [method write_to_dictionary] on export, and read back with [method read_from_dictionary]. Derived classes will usually define their own [code]from_dictionary[/code] static functions, which will construct instances and call [method read_from_dictionary]. You can extend a glTF item with additional properties by using [method get_additional_data] and [method set_additional_data].

method.name: _read_from_dictionary
method.description: Callback method that should read custom keys from the [Dictionary]. Do not call this method directly. This can be overridden in derived classes when creating a custom [GLTFItem] type in GDScript or another scripting language. See [method read_from_dictionary] for details.

method.name: _write_to_dictionary
method.description: Callback method that should write custom keys to the [Dictionary]. Do not call this method directly. This can be overridden in derived classes when creating a custom [GLTFItem] type in GDScript or another scripting language. See [method write_to_dictionary] for details.

method.name: get_additional_data
method.description: Gets additional arbitrary data in this [GLTFItem] instance. This can be used to keep per-item state data in [GLTFDocumentExtension] classes, which is important because they are stateless. The [param extension_name] is used as a key to store the data, and is generally the name of the [GLTFDocumentExtension] class, which is not necessarily the same as the name of the extension in the glTF file. If nothing was set, the return value is [code]null[/code].

method.name: has_additional_data
method.description: Checks if this [GLTFItem] instance has additional data set for the given extension name. If nothing was set, the return value is [code]false[/code].

method.name: read_from_dictionary
method.description: Reads glTF properties from the given [Dictionary] and applies them to this item. In [GLTFItem] itself, this considers the [code]"name"[/code] and [code]"extras"[/code] keys. The [code]"extras"[/code] key is copied to the [Object] metadata, which can be retrieved with [code].get_meta("extras")[/code]. Derived classes can read and apply more keys as needed. Custom classes can implement [method _read_from_dictionary] to handle custom keys. [b]Note:[/b] This function supports being re-run to apply overrides from the given [Dictionary]. As long as a first pass has properly initialized the object, it is able to handle partial dictionaries and will usually not fail if some required keys are missing. The [code]from_dictionary[/code] static functions on individual derived classes should be used instead when constructing a new object, as they usually check for required keys and will usually fail if given incomplete data. [b]Note:[/b] If the return value is not [constant OK], the data of the object may now be in an invalid state, with partially applied changes. If this happens, user code either needs to validate and fix it, discard/replace the broken object, or propagate the error to abort the entire glTF file import.

method.name: set_additional_data
method.description: Sets additional arbitrary data in this [GLTFItem] instance. This can be used to keep per-item state data in [GLTFDocumentExtension] classes, which is important because they are stateless. The [param extension_name] is used as a key to store the data, and is generally the name of the [GLTFDocumentExtension] class, which is not necessarily the same as the name of the extension in the glTF file. The [param additional_data] value can be any type.

method.name: write_to_dictionary
method.description: Writes the data of this [GLTFItem] to a [Dictionary] of glTF properties. In [GLTFItem] itself, only the [code]"name"[/code] and [code]"extras"[/code] keys are handled. Derived classes can write more keys as needed. Custom classes can implement [method _write_to_dictionary] for custom keys.
